hero.title: Build a vocabulary you can actually use
hero.description: FluentStellar is a multilingual vocabulary-learning platform designed to help you do more than recognize words. Through interactive exercises, guided learning, and regular review, you can develop your vocabulary, strengthen your memory, and make steady progress at your own pace.

approach.title: Learning words is only the beginning
approach.intro: Recognizing a word in a list is different from remembering it when you need it. That's why FluentStellar focuses on active participation instead of passive memorization. Our approach brings together three essential parts of vocabulary learning.

activeRecall.title: Remember words actively
activeRecall.body: Rather than simply reading translations or selecting familiar answers, you practice recalling words from memory. This encourages you to think, remember their spelling, and gradually become more confident with vocabulary you've encountered.

repetition.title: Strengthen what you've learned
repetition.body: Learning a word once doesn't mean you'll remember it forever. Regular reviews bring previously studied vocabulary back into practice, while spaced repetition helps you revisit words over time and reinforce your knowledge.

meaningfulUse.title: Practice in different ways
meaningfulUse.body: Different exercises challenge different aspects of your vocabulary knowledge. Writing complete words, filling in missing letters, assembling word fragments, matching meanings, and listening to pronunciation keep practice varied and engaging.

paths.title: Two ways to build your vocabulary
paths.intro: Whether you want a quick practice session or a structured learning routine, FluentStellar lets you choose an approach that fits your goals. You can start immediately without registering or create a free account for personalized learning.

customPractice.title: Custom Practice
customPractice.description: Take control of your vocabulary practice. Choose the languages you want to work with, focus on specific vocabulary, and select the exercises you enjoy most. There's no fixed session length, so you can practice for a few minutes or continue for as long as you like.

highlights.chooseLanguages: Choose your native language and the language you want to practice
highlights.chooseFilters: Focus on vocabulary by CEFR level, topic, or word type
highlights.flexibleSessions: Combine exercises and finish whenever you want

personalizedLearning.title: Personalized Learning
personalizedLearning.description: Build your vocabulary through a guided learning system that introduces new words and helps you retain them. Study vocabulary step by step, review previously learned words using spaced repetition, and follow your progress as your personal vocabulary grows.

highlights.guidedNewWords: Discover new words with definitions, examples, and guided exercises
highlights.spacedReview: Revisit studied vocabulary through spaced repetition
highlights.progressTracking: Set daily goals and track your vocabulary and learning progress

platform.title: Built around the way you learn
platform.intro: FluentStellar combines flexible practice with useful learning tools, so you can explore new vocabulary, organize the words that matter to you, and keep improving over time.

languagesLevels.title: Seven languages, six CEFR levels
languagesLevels.body: Explore vocabulary in English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, and Russian, with words organized across CEFR levels A1 to C2. Find vocabulary suited to your current knowledge or challenge yourself with more advanced words.

exercisesPronunciation.title: Interactive exercises and pronunciation
exercisesPronunciation.body: Move beyond reading word lists with exercises that develop spelling, recall, recognition, and listening. Listen to word pronunciation and practice vocabulary through several different types of challenges.

listsFavorites.title: Personal word lists and favorites
listsFavorites.body: Collect useful or difficult words in your own vocabulary lists, mark important words as favorites, and create focused practice sessions using the vocabulary you've selected.

progressReviews.title: Progress that builds over time
progressReviews.body: Keep track of studied words, review activity, daily learning goals, and vocabulary growth. Return to previously learned words, recognize your milestones, and see how your efforts add up.

cta.title: Your next word starts here
cta.description: You don't need to wait for the perfect learning plan. Start practicing vocabulary right away without an account, or create a free account to build a personalized learning routine and track your progress.

step1.title: Step 1: Choose languages
step1.item2: the language you want to practice

step2.title: Step 2: Set filters (optional)
step2.note2: By default, all filters are active.
step2.note3: If you do not select anything, it means you practice all levels, all topics, and all word types.

step3.title: Step 3: Choose exercises
step3.intro: Go to the exercise selection page and choose which exercise types you want to practice.
step3.note: By default, all exercises are selected.

step4.title: Step 4: Choose session size (optional)
step4.intro: You can choose how many words you want to practice in the session.
step4.item1: You can set a word quantity
step4.item2: Or start practicing without a limit and finish the session at any time

fullWord.title: 1) Full word typing
fullWord.goal: Goal: Type the correct word in the language you are practicing.
fullWord.seeInput: An input field where you type the answer

halfWritten.title: 2) Half-written word typing
halfWritten.goal: Goal: Complete a partially written word in the language you are practicing.
halfWritten.seePartial: The target word shown partially written (you must type the missing part)
halfWritten.seeInput: An input field for completing the missing letters
halfWritten.note: This exercise has no Hint button, because part of the word is already provided.

brokenWord.title: 3) Broken-word assembling
brokenWord.goal: Goal: Assemble the correct word by placing word parts in the correct order.
brokenWord.seeSlots: Empty slots for the word parts
brokenWord.seeChunks: A set of shuffled word parts that you place into the slots

connectWords.title: 4) Word connection
connectWords.goal: Goal: Connect words in the practicing language with their meanings in your native language.
connectWords.seeTypeTop: Word type (part of speech) at the top (applies to all items)
connectWords.seeLeft: Left side: 4 words in the language you are practicing
connectWords.seeRight: Right side: 4 meanings in your native language
connectWords.how1: Tap one item on the left, then tap the matching item on the right
connectWords.how3: Incorrect matches are highlighted briefly and can be retried

listening.title: 5) Listening exercise
listening.goal: Goal: Match spoken words in the practicing language with their meanings in your native language.
listening.seeTypeTop: Word type (part of speech) at the top (applies to all items)
listening.seeLeft: Left side: 4 audio buttons (microphone) for words in the practicing language
listening.seeRight: Right side: 4 meanings in your native language
listening.how1: Tap an audio button to hear a word
listening.how2: Then connect it to the correct meaning on the right
listening.how4: Incorrect matches are highlighted briefly and can be retried
listening.note: There are no hints and no "show me word" here.

common.seeMeaning: The word meaning in your native language
common.seeMeta: Word metadata: CEFR level, topic, and word type (part of speech)

finish.title: Skipping and finishing
finish.p1: Every exercise includes a Skip button.
finish.p2: You can finish the session at any time.
finish.p3: Words are counted only when you recall them correctly (revealing a word does not count as a successful recall).

page.title: Help Center
page.subtitle: Learn how to practice vocabulary, study new words, review what you've learned, and track your progress with FluentStellar.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.intro: FluentStellar offers two ways to build your vocabulary: practice freely without an account, or create an account to follow a personalized learning system.

choosePath.title: Choosing how to learn
choosePath.body:
Choose Custom Practice if you want to work on vocabulary at your own pace, with your preferred languages, exercises, and word filters.

Choose Personalized Learning if you want a structured way to study new words, review previously studied vocabulary, and track your progress over time.

withoutAccount.title: Practicing without an account
withoutAccount.body:
You can start practicing immediately without signing up. Select your languages, customize the vocabulary and exercises if you wish, and begin. Practice sessions have no word limit, so you can finish whenever you choose.

Your practice settings are remembered in your browser, but guest sessions and results are not saved to your account.

withAccount.title: Creating an account for personalized learning
withAccount.body:
Create a free account using Google or your email address. After signing in, complete your profile by choosing your languages and current vocabulary level.

Your account gives you access to Study New Words, Review Words, personal vocabulary lists, and learning statistics. Your progress is saved automatically as you study and review.

customPractice.title: Custom Practice
customPractice.intro: Custom Practice lets you practice vocabulary in any of the supported languages, using the exercises and word categories you choose. No account is required.

languages.title: Choosing languages
languages.body:
Choose Your language for the meanings and translations you will see, then choose Practice language for the words you want to learn. The two languages must be different.

You can swap the languages using the switch button. Your choices are remembered in your browser.

filters.title: Vocabulary filters
filters.body:
Use Customize Filters to select CEFR levels (A1–C2), vocabulary topics, or word types such as nouns, verbs, and adjectives. You can select several options in each category.

All filters are optional. If you leave a category unselected, vocabulary from every option in that category is included. Apply your filters to return to the practice setup.

exerciseSelection.title: Choosing exercises
exerciseSelection.body:
Choose which of the five exercise types you want to use. All five are selected by default, and you must keep at least one selected.

You can combine typing, word assembly, matching, and listening exercises. During practice, FluentStellar automatically uses the selected exercises that are suitable for the available words.

sessions.title: Practice sessions and finishing
sessions.body:
Press Start Practicing to begin. There is no fixed session length or word limit: you can continue as long as you like and press Finish whenever you are ready. Words may appear again as you continue practicing.

You can use Skip, request help where available, or choose Show me word when you cannot recall an answer. The finish screen summarizes your attempts, accuracy, performance by level and word type, and practiced words.

Custom Practice does not update your learned-word status or spaced-repetition schedule. If you are signed in, your active practice time contributes to Study Activity, but practice results do not count toward your daily new-word goal.

exerciseTypes.title: Exercise types
exerciseTypes.intro: FluentStellar offers five interactive exercise types. You can select the ones you prefer before starting Custom Practice.

wordTyping.title: Word typing
wordTyping.body:
Read the meaning in your language and type the complete word in the language you are practicing. You can listen to the pronunciation and view additional word information.

Use Hint to reveal some letters if you need help, or Show me word to see the answer. Accents and special characters must be entered correctly.

halfWritten.title: Half-written word completion
halfWritten.body:
Part of the word is already provided. Type the missing letters to complete it correctly.

This exercise helps you recall spelling with some letters given as a starting point. There is no Hint button because part of the answer is already visible.

brokenWord.title: Broken word assembling
brokenWord.body:
The target word is divided into shuffled parts. Select the parts in the correct order to assemble the complete word.

You can use Hint for assistance or Show me word to reveal the answer when needed.

connectWords.title: Connect words
connectWords.body:
Match four words in your practice language with their meanings in your own language. Select a word, then select its matching meaning.

Correct matches stay connected. If a pair is incorrect, you can try again.

listening.title: Listening
listening.body:
Listen to the spoken words and match each one with the correct meaning in your language. Use the audio buttons to hear the words before choosing their matches.

Audio uses your browser's speech feature, so pronunciation and voice availability may vary by device. If listening is unavailable, you can switch to Connect words during the session.

personalizedLearning.title: Personalized Learning
personalizedLearning.intro: With a FluentStellar account, you can follow a structured vocabulary-learning system that introduces new words, brings previously studied words back for review, and tracks your progress.

studyNewWords.title: Study New Words
studyNewWords.body:
Open Learning and select Study New Words. FluentStellar chooses new vocabulary from its organized learning sequence, starting at your selected CEFR level and excluding words you have already studied.

Each word begins with its meaning, definition, example sentence, and pronunciation. You then practice it through three exercises: Broken word, Half-written word completion, and Word typing.

A word is saved to your vocabulary after you complete all three exercises. You can finish the session early; words already completed remain saved, while an unfinished word is not saved.

reviewWords.title: Review Words
reviewWords.body:
Review Words helps you strengthen vocabulary you have already studied. FluentStellar uses spaced repetition to bring words back over time, while also including additional studied words that may not yet be due for review.

Correct answers help words progress toward mastery, while incorrect answers indicate that more practice is needed. Reviews are saved automatically after each word.

Review sessions have no fixed word limit. You can continue reviewing as long as words are available and finish whenever you choose.

dailyGoal.title: Daily Learning Goal
dailyGoal.body:
Your daily learning goal determines how many new words you aim to study each day. You can choose a goal of 10, 15, 20, 30, or 50 words from the Learning section. The default is 15.

Only completed new words count toward this goal. Reviewing words and using Custom Practice do not increase your daily new-word count. Reaching your goal contributes to your Daily Streak.

After completing your goal, you can continue reviewing vocabulary. To study additional new words on the same day, you can increase your daily goal.

learningProgress.title: How Vocabulary Progress Works
learningProgress.body: Your studied words move through Learning, Known, and Mastered as you answer reviews over time. A correct review can strengthen a word; an incorrect answer can move it back. New words first enter Learning, even when you needed help during their introduction. You can see these categories in Vocabulary. Your learning progress is saved automatically and kept separately for each learning language.

myLists.title: My Lists
myLists.intro: Create personal collections of vocabulary you want to keep together, whether you have studied those words already or not.

manageLists.title: Creating and managing lists
manageLists.body: Open My Lists in your profile and select Create List. Give your list a name, then open it to see or manage its words. You can search, sort, rename, or delete lists. Each learning language has its own lists, so changing languages shows the lists for that language.

addWords.title: Adding and removing words
addWords.body: Inside a list, choose Add Words to search the vocabulary collection and select words to include. You can also add words from your Vocabulary collection, supported session-finish screens, or public full vocabulary lists after signing in. Remove a word from a list whenever you like; this does not delete your learning progress. A word can belong to several lists.

practiceList.title: Practicing a list
practiceList.body: Open a list and select Practice List. Choose how many words to draw from that list, whether to use random or list order, and which exercises to include. The selected words run in a flexible practice session that continues until you finish. List practice uses Custom Practice, so it does not change your spaced-repetition progress or daily new-word goal.

vocabularyProgress.title: Vocabulary & Progress
vocabularyProgress.intro: Your profile brings together the words you have studied, their current learning status, and an overview of your activity.

vocabulary.title: Vocabulary collection
vocabulary.body: Open Vocabulary to browse the words you have completed in Study New Words. Search for a word or filter the collection by level, word type, or learning status. You can open word details, add words to a personal list, and see when a word was last practiced. Words practiced only in Custom Practice do not automatically enter this collection.

statuses.title: Learning, Known, and Mastered
statuses.body: Learning contains words you have recently started or are still strengthening. Known contains words you have recalled successfully through further reviews. Mastered contains words you have retained through more advanced review stages. These statuses can change as you continue reviewing. In My Lists, Not studied identifies words you have saved to a list but have not yet learned through Study New Words.

favorites.title: Favorites
favorites.body: Use the star in Vocabulary or supported learning-session word lists to mark words as Favorites. Open the Favorites tab in Vocabulary to find them again. Favorites organize your studied words; they do not change review schedules.

dashboard.title: Dashboard and statistics
dashboard.body: Dashboard shows today’s new-word progress, your daily goal, streak, vocabulary overview, study activity, and recent learning. Study Activity includes active Custom Practice time for signed-in users. Use the Learning section to start a new-word or review session.

milestones.title: Milestones and vocabulary growth
milestones.body: Open Progress to see milestones for learning, known words, mastery, reviews, and consistency. The Vocabulary Growth chart shows how your studied vocabulary has developed over time. The Consistency milestone counts days with new-word study or reviews; it is different from the Daily Streak, which depends on meeting your daily new-word goal.

resources.title: Explore & Learning Resources
resources.intro: Explore vocabulary and language references freely, with no account required. These resources can help you find words to practice or add to personal lists.

explore.title: Vocabulary Explorer
explore.body: Open Explore to choose one of the seven languages and browse its available vocabulary pages, tests, and verb resources. Explore is a directory of learning materials; it is not the same as your personal Vocabulary collection in your profile.

cefr.title: CEFR vocabulary resources
cefr.body: Browse vocabulary by CEFR level, from A1 to C2, to focus on words appropriate to different stages of learning. You can also browse full vocabulary lists across levels. On supported level pages, the practice link opens Custom Practice with that level already selected.

wordDetails.title: Word details and pronunciation
wordDetails.body: Open a word to see its translation, definition, example sentence, pronunciation, and available grammar information, including word type and CEFR level. Some word pages also include a short typing check and related vocabulary. Audio uses the speech voices available in your browser or device.

verbs.title: Verb reference resources
verbs.body: Learning Resources includes collections of common verbs, and where available, past forms and conjugation references. Use these pages to look up verb forms and discover vocabulary you want to practice.

levelTest.title: Vocabulary Level Test
levelTest.body:
Take the free Vocabulary Level Test to get an approximate indication of your vocabulary level. It starts with easier levels and progresses toward harder ones. Early questions ask you to recognize a translation; later questions ask you to assemble a word from parts. The test stops when you make too many mistakes at a level.

The result is an estimate, not a certified CEFR assessment. Choosing Start Practicing at This Level applies the level to Custom Practice filters; it does not automatically change your account’s current level. You can change that separately in Settings.

accountSettings.title: Account & Settings
accountSettings.intro: Manage your account details, learning preferences, and personal data from Settings in your profile.

registration.title: Registration and sign-in
registration.body: Select Log In, then choose the option to create an account. You can sign up with Google or with an email address and password. Email registrations require you to confirm your address before signing in. If you forget your password, use Forgot password? on the login form.

profileSetup.title: Profile setup
profileSetup.body: At your first sign-in, complete the required profile information: nickname, native language, learning language, current CEFR level, age, and birth month and day. Your daily new-word goal starts at 15 words and can be changed later in Learning. The Vocabulary Level Test is optional and is not part of registration.

languages.title: Changing learning languages and level
languages.body: Go to Settings → Languages to change your native language, learning language, or current level. Your current level controls the starting point for Study New Words; changing it does not erase words you have already studied. Progress and lists are kept separately for each learning language. Your daily goal and current level are shared account settings, so check them when switching languages.

timezone.title: Time zone
timezone.body: Choose your time zone under Settings → Time & Region. It determines when a new learning day starts for daily goals, streaks, and statistics. If you travel or move, update it to keep your learning day aligned with your local time.

resetProgress.title: Resetting learning progress
resetProgress.body: In Settings → Data & Account, you can permanently reset learning progress for the currently selected learning language. This removes that language’s studied-word progress, favorites, review history, streaks, daily statistics, and Custom Practice history. Other learning languages and your account remain. The action requires you to type RESET and cannot be undone.

deleteAccount.title: Deleting an account
deleteAccount.body: In Settings → Data & Account, you can permanently delete your account and its associated data. This is different from resetting the progress of one language. You must confirm by typing DELETE; email-and-password accounts must also enter their password. Account deletion cannot be undone.

accountRequired.question: Do I need an account?
accountRequired.answer: No. You can use Custom Practice, the Vocabulary Level Test, Explore, and public Learning Resources without signing in. An account is required for Study New Words, Review Words, personal lists, and saved learning progress.

practiceProgress.question: Does Custom Practice save my progress?
practiceProgress.answer: Custom Practice does not save individual words as learned or update their review schedules. Guests do not have account-saved results. When you are signed in, active Custom Practice time contributes to your Study Activity statistics, but the words do not count toward your daily new-word goal or mastery.

reviewSystem.question: How does Review Words work?
reviewSystem.answer: After you study new words, Review Words brings them back for practice. Your answers affect their learning status and when they are scheduled again. The session can include both overdue words and other previously studied words, and you can finish whenever you want.

changeLanguage.question: Can I change my learning language?
changeLanguage.answer: Yes. Open Settings → Languages to choose another learning language. Vocabulary progress and personal lists are kept separately for each language, so changing languages does not erase your previous work. Check your current level after switching, because it is an account-wide setting.

audio.question: Why isn't audio playing?
audio.answer: FluentStellar uses the speech voices provided by your browser and device. Check that your sound is on, try the pronunciation button again, and confirm that your browser supports speech synthesis. If a voice for your practice language is unavailable, try another browser or device. In a Listening exercise, you can switch to Connect words.

finishSession.question: Can I finish a session at any time?
finishSession.answer: Yes. Custom Practice and Review Words allow you to finish whenever you choose. Study New Words also lets you finish early; words you already completed are saved, but the current unfinished word is not. Practice List sessions can also be ended whenever you want.
